messages:
maria: Heads up — PayFlux (dedicated tenant) pinged support: 5xx/latency spikes around 15:12 PDT. They see a pattern of scale down → scale up churn and client 429s.

jake: I picked this up from the alert too. Autoscaler logs show pool dp-nyc-4c went from 6 -> 2 -> 6 between 15:10-15:18. Metric source: request_queue_depth oscillating between 5 and 0.

sophia: Any noisy-job signals? Could be one tenant doing big batch runs that drain capacity then idle.

maria: Support said they didn't change workload, just higher tail latency. I asked for a short repro trace and example request ids. They sent request ids: rf-7a3c, rf-7a3d.

jake: pulled logs, here's an excerpt from the autoscaler: 

```
2026-03-16T15:09:52Z autoscaler: pool=dp-nyc-4c desired=6 cur=6 queue=5
2026-03-16T15:12:02Z autoscaler: pool=dp-nyc-4c desired=2 cur=6 cooldown=30s reason=low_queue
2026-03-16T15:13:10Z autoscaler: pool=dp-nyc-4c desired=6 cur=2 reason=queue_spike
```

alan: That cooldown looks short. We recently reduced cooldown to 30s in the late-Feb tuning experiment. Might be too aggressive for bursty workloads.

sophia: Agreed. Also saw eviction logs on one GPU host around 15:11 — OOM killer fired, and several workers restarted at once. Could be a noisy neighbor forcing pod restarts which drop available capacity suddenly.

maria: client trace (rf-7a3c) shows 429s at 15:12:13 with header x-retry-after: 10s. They retried and then saw timeouts.

sre-bot: Incident note created: INC-20260316-4321. Pager duty alert suppressed for 10m.

jake: Immediate mitigation options: 1) bump autoscaler cooldown to 120s for dedicated pools, 2) add hysteresis on queue metric (require sustained queue > threshold for 2 windows), 3) isolate suspected noisy host (cordon + migrate). Which should we try first?

alan: Do 1+2 as config change ASAP. 3 requires host-level investigation and can cause churn.

sophia: I can cordon one suspect node (host-nyc-11) after hours if we get repro. For now let's adjust cooldown to 120s and enable sliding window.

maria: I updated the autoscaler policy draft in the console: cooldown_seconds: 120, queue_hysteresis_windows: 2. Rolling deploy to canary pools now.

jake: Can you paste the curl to test queue metric sim? I'll run a load generator against a canary pool.

sophia: Sure — use the internal chaos endpoint to push simulated prefix loads: 

curl -X POST "https://internal-api.redwood/test/load" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $INTERNAL_TOKEN" \ 
  -d '{"pool":"dp-nyc-4c-canary","qps":200,"duration_s":60}'

jake: Kicking off load now against canary. Will watch autoscaler decisions and pod restarts.

(10m pass)

jake: Canary ran: queue rose to ~18 then decayed; autoscaler kept desired at 6 thanks to the 120s cooldown. No bounce observed. Client 429s didn't reproduce in the canary.

maria: Support notified PayFlux of config change and asked them to rerun their workload during their next window.

sophia: For follow-up: we should add a detection rule for rapid scale-down events (e.g., desired drop >=50% in <2m) and auto-flag for host-level investigation. Also run an offline job to scan for processes that spike memory on hosts.

alan: Filing a follow-up RFC to make 120s default for dedicated pools + metric hysteresis. Also adding a runbook step to inspect GPU eviction logs when a scale event occurs.

maria: Thanks team — I'll keep monitoring INC-20260316-4321 and update when PayFlux confirms.

jake: TL;DR: root cause appears to be overly-aggressive cooldown + transient noisy-host evictions. Mitigation: increased cooldown/hysteresis prevented churn in canary. Next: host-level sweeps and RFC. :thumbsup:
